From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: AllyBridge MSA v2 + SOW draft (redlines attached)

Vanessa / Kim — forwarding AllyBridge redlines. Key asks from procurement are on data processing persistence and subprocessors. Procurement wants a clear yes/no on persistence and an ETA for subprocessor list.

My thoughts: we should be able to confirm no persistent customer data is stored beyond KV cache lifetime and provide a templated subprocessor list; the DPA language AllyBridge proposes is slightly broader than our standard. Would prefer we push back on their requirement for "prior written consent" for any subprocessor changes and offer a 30-day notice + objection window instead.

Can you advise: 1) is the "no persistence" statement defensible given our caching and KV behavior? 2) if legal agrees to 30-day notice, is procurement likely to accept?

I attached a quick counterproposal (Redwood_Counterproposal_0524.pdf) that I drafted — feel free to edit.

—Jordan
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AllyBridge MSA v2 + SOW draft (redlines attached)

Jordan / Vanessa — quick answers from security/legal intake perspective:

- Persistence: we do not persist raw customer payloads beyond the request lifecycle. We maintain ephemeral KV cache for latency improvements; entries are evicted on LRU or TTL and are not stored to durable storage in plaintext. We can add a sentence clarifying that cached tokens are ephemeral and encrypted in memory, and that long-term logs retain only metadata and aggregated telemetry (no full request bodies).

- Subprocessors: we can provide the current list and agree to a 30-day notice before onboarding a new subprocessor. "Prior written consent" is high friction for procurement at their scale; 30-day notice + objection with defined grounds is standard.

I'll mark up the DPA language in the counterproposal and return by EOD. If procurement needs SOC 2 artifacts, we can share a redacted report under NDA.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya.r@allybridge.com>; AllyBridge Legal <legal@allybridge.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal + clarification on caching and subprocessors

Maya — thanks for the redlines. Quick summary of our position: 

1) Data persistence: Redwood does NOT persist customer request payloads to durable storage. We use an in-memory KV cache for performance; entries are encrypted in memory and evicted per TTL/LRU. We will add explicit language to the DPA: "Redwood does not persist customer request payloads beyond the request processing lifecycle; ephemeral caches are retained only for performance reasons and are encrypted in memory."

2) Subprocessors: attached is our counterproposal that replaces "prior written consent" with a 30-day notice and objection process and commits to providing a current subprocessor list at signature and updates thereafter.

Attached: Redwood_Counterproposal_0524.pdf; SOW-Data-Connector_v1.xlsx (with minor scope clarifications). Can you confirm whether AllyBridge procurement requires any additional export/control language or if the contract team is comfortable with the notice model?

If procurement is OK, we're happy to proceed to DocuSign and MSAsigned + SOW PO.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
From: AllyBridge Legal <legal@allybridge.com>

Date: 2027-05-22T13:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal + clarification on caching and subprocessors

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the counterproposal. We appreciate the clarified language on ephemeral caching. A couple of small asks from legal/procurement side before we move to signature:

• Can Redwood quantify the TTL range for KV entries (e.g., typical TTLs are 5–30 minutes for the connector use case)? We don't need an exact SLA but a typical range to include in the SOW appendix helps procurement.
• For the subprocessor notice, AllyBridge's standard is 30 days but with the right to suspend new integrations if a material data protection concern is raised; would Redwood accept the ability for AllyBridge to suspend new subprocessor onboarding pending remediation?

If you can accept both items, procurement will prepare the PO and send for signature. We prefer to use DocuSign (link will follow).

Regards,

Elena Park
Senior Counsel, AllyBridge Legal
legal@allybridge.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: AllyBridge Legal <legal@allybridge.com>, Maya R. <maya.r@allybridge.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counterproposal + clarification on caching and subprocessors

Elena / Maya — all good from our side. Responses below and attached final mark-up:

• TTL range: typical KV TTL for connector requests is 2–20 minutes depending on traffic patterns; we'll include a non-normative appendix in the SOW with a 2–20 minute typical range and note that extreme burst scenarios may transiently exceed that window but eviction remains automatic and non-durable.

• Subprocessor suspension: Redwood can accept AllyBridge's right to suspend onboarding of a new subprocessor on reasonable, material data-protection grounds, provided that: (i) AllyBridge provides written notice with specific grounds; (ii) Redwood has a 15-business-day cure period to remediate or propose mitigations; and (iii) suspension is narrowly tailored to the specific onboarding activity. This preserves procurement's ability to pause while giving Redwood a path to address issues.

Attached: Redwood_Counterproposal_0524.pdf (final mark-up). Once procurement shares the DocuSign link we'll execute. Looking forward to the integration kickoff.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Partner Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Counterproposal_0524.pdf, SOW-Data-Connector_v1.xlsx
